From 90f9f5d64cae4e72defd96a2a22760173cb3c9ec Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Steven Rostedt <rostedt@goodmis.org>
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 19:48:24 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] tracing: Fix crash on synthetic stacktrace field usage

When creating a synthetic event based on an existing synthetic event that
had a stacktrace field and the new synthetic event used that field a
kernel crash occurred:

 ~# cd /sys/kernel/tracing
 ~# echo 's:stack unsigned long stack[];' > dynamic_events
 ~# echo 'hist:keys=prev_pid:s0=common_stacktrace if prev_state & 3' >> events/sched/sched_switch/trigger
 ~# echo 'hist:keys=next_pid:s1=$s0:onmatch(sched.sched_switch).trace(stack,$s1)' >> events/sched/sched_switch/trigger

The above creates a synthetic event that takes a stacktrace when a task
schedules out in a non-running state and passes that stacktrace to the
sched_switch event when that task schedules back in. It triggers the
"stack" synthetic event that has a stacktrace as its field (called "stack").

 ~# echo 's:syscall_stack s64 id; unsigned long stack[];' >> dynamic_events
 ~# echo 'hist:keys=common_pid:s2=stack' >> events/synthetic/stack/trigger
 ~# echo 'hist:keys=common_pid:s3=$s2,i0=id:onmatch(synthetic.stack).trace(syscall_stack,$i0,$s3)' >> events/raw_syscalls/sys_exit/trigger

The above makes another synthetic event called "syscall_stack" that
attaches the first synthetic event (stack) to the sys_exit trace event and
records the stacktrace from the stack event with the id of the system call
that is exiting.

When enabling this event (or using it in a historgram):

 ~# echo 1 > events/synthetic/syscall_stack/enable

Produces a kernel crash!

 BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: 0000000000400010
 #PF: supervisor read access in kernel mode
 #PF: error_code(0x0000) - not-present page
 PGD 0 P4D 0
 Oops: Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP PTI
 CPU: 6 UID: 0 PID: 1257 Comm: bash Not tainted 6.16.3+deb14-amd64 #1 PREEMPT(lazy)  Debian 6.16.3-1
 Hardware name: QEMU Standard PC (Q35 + ICH9, 2009), BIOS 1.17.0-debian-1.17.0-1 04/01/2014
 RIP: 0010:trace_event_raw_event_synth+0x90/0x380
 Code: c5 00 00 00 00 85 d2 0f 84 e1 00 00 00 31 db eb 34 0f 1f 00 66 66 2e 0f 1f 84 00 00 00 00 00 66 66 2e 0f 1f 84 00 00 00 00 00 <49> 8b 04 24 48 83 c3 01 8d 0c c5 08 00 00 00 01 cd 41 3b 5d 40 0f
 RSP: 0018:ffffd2670388f958 EFLAGS: 00010202
 RAX: ffff8ba1065cc100 RBX: 0000000000000000 RCX: 0000000000000000
 RDX: 0000000000000001 RSI: fffff266ffda7b90 RDI: ffffd2670388f9b0
 RBP: 0000000000000010 R08: ffff8ba104e76000 R09: ffffd2670388fa50
 R10: ffff8ba102dd42e0 R11: ffffffff9a908970 R12: 0000000000400010
 R13: ffff8ba10a246400 R14: ffff8ba10a710220 R15: fffff266ffda7b90
 FS:  00007fa3bc63f740(0000) GS:ffff8ba2e0f48000(0000) knlGS:0000000000000000
 CS:  0010 DS: 0000 ES: 0000 CR0: 0000000080050033
 CR2: 0000000000400010 CR3: 0000000107f9e003 CR4: 0000000000172ef0
 Call Trace:
  <TASK>
  ? __tracing_map_insert+0x208/0x3a0
  action_trace+0x67/0x70
  event_hist_trigger+0x633/0x6d0
  event_triggers_call+0x82/0x130
  trace_event_buffer_commit+0x19d/0x250
  trace_event_raw_event_sys_exit+0x62/0xb0
  syscall_exit_work+0x9d/0x140
  do_syscall_64+0x20a/0x2f0
  ? trace_event_raw_event_sched_switch+0x12b/0x170
  ? save_fpregs_to_fpstate+0x3e/0x90
  ? _raw_spin_unlock+0xe/0x30
  ? finish_task_switch.isra.0+0x97/0x2c0
  ? __rseq_handle_notify_resume+0xad/0x4c0
  ? __schedule+0x4b8/0xd00
  ? restore_fpregs_from_fpstate+0x3c/0x90
  ? switch_fpu_return+0x5b/0xe0
  ? do_syscall_64+0x1ef/0x2f0
  ? do_fault+0x2e9/0x540
  ? __handle_mm_fault+0x7d1/0xf70
  ? count_memcg_events+0x167/0x1d0
  ? handle_mm_fault+0x1d7/0x2e0
  ? do_user_addr_fault+0x2c3/0x7f0
  entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x76/0x7e

The reason is that the stacktrace field is not labeled as such, and is
treated as a normal field and not as a dynamic event that it is.

In trace_event_raw_event_synth() the event is field is still treated as a
dynamic array, but the retrieval of the data is considered a normal field,
and the reference is just the meta data:

// Meta data is retrieved instead of a dynamic array
  str_val = (char *)(long)var_ref_vals[val_idx];

// Then when it tries to process it:
  len = *((unsigned long *)str_val) + 1;

It triggers a kernel page fault.

To fix this, first when defining the fields of the first synthetic event,
set the filter type to FILTER_STACKTRACE. This is used later by the second
synthetic event to know that this field is a stacktrace. When creating
the field of the new synthetic event, have it use this FILTER_STACKTRACE
to know to create a stacktrace field to copy the stacktrace into.

Cc: Masami Hiramatsu <mhiramat@kernel.org>
Cc: Mathieu Desnoyers <mathieu.desnoyers@efficios.com>
Cc: Tom Zanussi <zanussi@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260122194824.6905a38e@gandalf.local.home
Fixes: 00cf3d672a9d ("tracing: Allow synthetic events to pass around stacktraces")
Signed-off-by: Steven Rostedt (Google) <rostedt@goodmis.org>

diff --git a/kernel/trace/trace_events_hist.c b/kernel/trace/trace_events_hist.c
index 5e6e70540eef..c97bb2fda5c0 100644
--- a/kernel/trace/trace_events_hist.c
+++ b/kernel/trace/trace_events_hist.c
@@ -2057,6 +2057,15 @@ static struct hist_field *create_hist_field(struct hist_trigger_data *hist_data,
 			hist_field->fn_num = HIST_FIELD_FN_RELDYNSTRING;
 		else
 			hist_field->fn_num = HIST_FIELD_FN_PSTRING;
+	} else if (field->filter_type == FILTER_STACKTRACE) {
+		flags |= HIST_FIELD_FL_STACKTRACE;
+
+		hist_field->size = MAX_FILTER_STR_VAL;
+		hist_field->type = kstrdup_const(field->type, GFP_KERNEL);
+		if (!hist_field->type)
+			goto free;
+
+		hist_field->fn_num = HIST_FIELD_FN_STACK;
 	} else {
 		hist_field->size = field->size;
 		hist_field->is_signed = field->is_signed;

diff --git a/kernel/trace/trace_events_synth.c b/kernel/trace/trace_events_synth.c
index 4554c458b78c..45c187e77e21 100644
--- a/kernel/trace/trace_events_synth.c
+++ b/kernel/trace/trace_events_synth.c
@@ -130,7 +130,9 @@ static int synth_event_define_fields(struct trace_event_call *call)
 	struct synth_event *event = call->data;
 	unsigned int i, size, n_u64;
 	char *name, *type;
+	int filter_type;
 	bool is_signed;
+	bool is_stack;
 	int ret = 0;
 
 	for (i = 0, n_u64 = 0; i < event->n_fields; i++) {
@@ -138,8 +140,12 @@ static int synth_event_define_fields(struct trace_event_call *call)
 		is_signed = event->fields[i]->is_signed;
 		type = event->fields[i]->type;
 		name = event->fields[i]->name;
+		is_stack = event->fields[i]->is_stack;
+
+		filter_type = is_stack ? FILTER_STACKTRACE : FILTER_OTHER;
+
 		ret = trace_define_field(call, type, name, offset, size,
-					 is_signed, FILTER_OTHER);
+					 is_signed, filter_type);
 		if (ret)
 			break;
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

The patch fixes a kernel crash when using synthetic events that pass stacktrace fields between events. The crash occurred because stacktrace fields in synthetic events were not properly identified as such, leading to incorrect memory access when processing them.

### Changes in `kernel/trace/trace_events_hist.c`
- **Added handling for `FILTER_STACKTRACE` fields in `create_hist_field()`**  
  When a field's filter type is `FILTER_STACKTRACE`, the function now sets the `HIST_FIELD_FL_STACKTRACE` flag, assigns an appropriate size (`MAX_FILTER_STR_VAL`), stores the field type, and sets the function number to `HIST_FIELD_FN_STACK`.  
  This ensures stacktrace fields are treated as dynamic arrays and processed correctly when creating histogram fields.

### Changes in `kernel/trace/trace_events_synth.c`
- **Propagated stacktrace flag to `filter_type` in `synth_event_define_fields()`**  
  For each field in a synthetic event, the function now checks if the field is a stacktrace (`is_stack`). If true, it uses `FILTER_STACKTRACE` as the `filter_type` parameter for `trace_define_field()`; otherwise, it uses `FILTER_OTHER`.  
  This ensures that the field's stacktrace nature is recorded in the event's metadata, enabling correct identification later.

### Relationship Between Changes
The crash originated because the second synthetic event did not recognize the field from the first synthetic event as a stacktrace.  
- **`trace_events_synth.c`** ensures that when defining fields for any synthetic event, the `filter_type` is set to `FILTER_STACKTRACE` for stacktrace fields.  
- **`trace_events_hist.c`** uses that `filter_type` during histogram field creation to properly handle stacktrace fields as dynamic arrays rather than normal fields.  

Together, these changes ensure that stacktrace fields are consistently identified and processed throughout the synthetic event creation and histogram registration pipeline, preventing the page fault caused by treating metadata as a valid data pointer.

2.34.1

The patch fixes a kernel crash when using synthetic events that reference stacktrace fields from other synthetic events. The modifications are in two files:

### `kernel/trace/trace_events_hist.c`
- In `create_hist_field()`, added a new condition to handle fields with `filter_type == FILTER_STACKTRACE`.  
  - Sets `HIST_FIELD_FL_STACKTRACE` flag.  
  - Sets `size` to `MAX_FILTER_STR_VAL` and copies the field type.  
  - Sets `fn_num` to `HIST_FIELD_FN_STACK`.  
  This ensures that when a synthetic event’s field is derived from a stacktrace field (e.g., from another synthetic event), it is correctly treated as a dynamic stacktrace array rather than a normal scalar field.

### `kernel/trace/trace_events_synth.c`
- In `synth_event_define_fields()`, added detection of the `is_stack` flag from each field.  
  - If `is_stack` is true, `filter_type` is set to `FILTER_STACKTRACE`; otherwise `FILTER_OTHER`.  
  - This `filter_type` is passed to `trace_define_field()`, so that the field’s format metadata correctly identifies it as a stacktrace.  

### Relationship between the changes
The crash occurred because fields derived from stacktraces were not marked as `FILTER_STACKTRACE` during synthetic event definition. As a result, when the hist trigger system later processed such a field via `create_hist_field()`, it treated it as a normal field (e.g., expecting a simple value), but the actual data was a dynamic stacktrace array, causing a page fault. The fix ensures that:  
1. The field definition tags stacktrace-derived fields with `FILTER_STACKTRACE`.  
2. The hist field creation recognizes this tag and sets up the proper handler (`HIST_FIELD_FN_STACK`) and size, preventing illegal memory access.  

Both changes together ensure consistent handling of stacktrace fields across synthetic event creation and hist trigger usage.

## Summary of Modifications

### File 1: `kernel/trace/trace_events_synth.c`
- **What changed**: In `synth_event_define_fields()`, the `filter_type` argument passed to `trace_define_field()` is now dynamically set to `FILTER_STACKTRACE` if the field being defined is a stack trace (based on the `is_stack` attribute of the field). Previously, it was always hardcoded to `FILTER_OTHER`.
- **Why**: This ensures that when a synthetic event contains a stacktrace field, the field is correctly marked with its proper filter type. Without this, the field appears as a regular field, leading to incorrect handling later.

### File 2: `kernel/trace/trace_events_hist.c`
- **What changed**: In `create_hist_field()`, a new condition is added that checks if a field’s `filter_type` is `FILTER_STACKTRACE`. If so, the field is initialized as a stacktrace hist field: flags get `HIST_FIELD_FL_STACKTRACE`, `hist_field->size` is set to `MAX_FILTER_STR_VAL`, `hist_field->type` is duplicated from the field’s type, and `hist_field->fn_num` is set to `HIST_FIELD_FN_STACK`.
- **Why**: When a second synthetic event references a stacktrace field from another synthetic event, this change ensures the histogram infrastructure treats it correctly as a dynamic array (stack) rather than a simple static field, preventing a page fault caused by misinterpreting the data.

### Relationship Between the Modifications
The two changes work together to fix the crash:
1. The first change (in trace_events_synth.c) properly tags stacktrace fields with `FILTER_STACKTRACE` during field definition.
2. The second change (in trace_events_hist.c) uses that tag to create an appropriate hist_field that understands how to access and handle stack trace data. Without the first change, the second change would never see `FILTER_STACKTRACE`; without the second change, the first change would have no effect on histogram operations. Together they ensure that stacktrace fields in synthetic events are correctly propagated and used in nested synthetic events and histograms.

Here is the root cause:
When defining fields for a synthetic event, the filter_type is always set to FILTER_OTHER, even for stacktrace fields. This prevents later code from recognizing the field as a stacktrace, causing it to be treated as a regular field and leading to a crash when accessing it as a dynamic array.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int synth_event_define_fields(struct trace_event_call *call)
 {
 	struct synth_trace_event trace;
 	int offset = offsetof(typeof(trace), fields);
 	struct synth_event *event = call->data;
 	unsigned int i, size, n_u64;
 	char *name, *type;
+	int filter_type;
 	bool is_signed;
+	bool is_stack;
 	int ret = 0;
 
 	for (i = 0, n_u64 = 0; i < event->n_fields; i++) {
 		size = event->fields[i]->size;
 		is_signed = event->fields[i]->is_signed;
 		type = event->fields[i]->type;
 		name = event->fields[i]->name;
+		is_stack = event->fields[i]->is_stack;
+
+		filter_type = is_stack ? FILTER_STACKTRACE : FILTER_OTHER;
+
 		ret = trace_define_field(call, type, name, offset, size,
-					 is_signed, FILTER_OTHER);
+					 is_signed, filter_type);
 		if (ret)
 			break;
 
 		event->fields[i]->offset = n_u64;
 
 		if (event->fields[i]->is_string && !event->fields[i]->is_dynamic) {
 			offset += STR_VAR_LEN_MAX;
 			n_u64 += STR_VAR_LEN_MAX / sizeof(u64);
 		} else {
 			offset += sizeof(u64);
 			n_u64++;
 		}
 	}
 
 	event->n_u64 = n_u64;
 
 	return ret;
 }
